condition: Emergency laparotomy in a frail older patient (NELA high risk) — perforated diverticulitis on apixaban
summary: 84-year-old frail woman (CFS 6) on apixaban with faecal peritonitis from perforated sigmoid diverticulitis, hypotensive with lactate 4.1 — emergency laparotomy.

inputs.hpi: 24 hours of generalised abdominal pain after 3 days of left-sided pain; vomiting, not passed urine since morning. Lives alone with twice-daily carers; needs help with bathing and shopping (CFS 6). Mild cognitive impairment. Atrial fibrillation on apixaban, last dose this morning.

exam.general: Drowsy but orientated, dry. HR 118 irregular, BP 94/58, RR 24, SpO2 94% on air, T 38.4°C.
exam.abdomen: Distended, rigid, generalised guarding and rebound. Absent bowel sounds.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis
imaging.result: Perforated sigmoid diverticulitis with free gas and generalised free fluid in keeping with faecal peritonitis.

inputs.socialHistory: Widowed, lives alone with carers twice daily. Non-smoker.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Perforated sigmoid diverticulitis with faecal peritonitis — emergency laparotomy (frail, on apixaban)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Perforated sigmoid diverticulitis, faecal peritonitis (Hinchey IV), sepsis with hypotension and lactate 4.1. Frail (CFS 6), 84, on apixaban. Emergency laparotomy (Hartmann's) after risk assessment and shared decision.

guideline.name: WSES guidelines — management of intra-abdominal infections
guideline.section: Early source control; CT for diagnosis; percutaneous drainage for accessible collections; relaparotomy for diffuse peritonitis; empirical antibiotics by severity and local resistance
guideline.citation: Sartelli M, Chichom-Mefire A, Labricciosa FM, et al. World J Emerg Surg. 2017;12:29.

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign — international guidelines 2021
guideline.section: Antimicrobials within 1 h for possible septic shock or high likelihood of sepsis; source control as soon as practical; measure lactate; admit to ICU when needed
guideline.citation: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Crit Care Med. 2021;49:e1063–143.

guideline.name: RCS England / DH — The higher risk general surgical patient
guideline.section: Estimate and document mortality risk before emergency surgery (e.g. P-POSSUM); predicted mortality ≥5%: consultant surgeon and anaesthetist present, post-operative critical care; ≥10%: consultant-delivered care
guideline.citation: Royal College of Surgeons of England, Department of Health. The higher risk general surgical patient: towards improved care for a forgotten group. London: RCS; 2011 (revised 2018).

guideline.name: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) — standards of care
guideline.section: Documented preoperative risk assessment (NELA/P-POSSUM), timely antibiotics and theatre, consultant surgeon and anaesthetist present for high-risk cases, post-operative critical care when predicted mortality ≥5%, frailty assessment and elderly medicine review for patients aged ≥65
guideline.citation: NELA Project Team. Ninth Patient Report of the National Emergency Laparotomy Audit. London: RCoA; 2023.

guideline.name: CPOC/BGS guideline — perioperative care for people living with frailty undergoing elective and emergency surgery
guideline.section: Frailty screening (Clinical Frailty Scale) for people aged ≥65; comprehensive geriatric assessment; cognitive and delirium risk assessment; shared decision-making including treatment escalation; post-operative delirium prevention
guideline.citation: Centre for Perioperative Care, British Geriatrics Society. London: CPOC; 2021.

guideline.name: 2022 ESC guidelines — cardiovascular assessment and management of patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery (with ESAIC)
guideline.section: Clinical risk (RCRI), functional capacity (e.g. climbing two flights of stairs); ECG and NT-proBNP/BNP and troponin in patients with risk factors before intermediate/high-risk surgery; echocardiography in poor functional capacity, raised NT-proBNP or known HF; delay elective surgery until 6 months after elective PCI and 12 months after ACS; continue aspirin after PCI if bleeding risk allows; interrupt P2Y12 inhibitors only in agreement with the cardiologist; bridging not recommended for antiplatelet interruption
guideline.citation: Halvorsen S, Mehilli J, Cassese S, et al. 2022 ESC Guidelines on cardiovascular assessment and management of patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery. Eur Heart J. 2022;43:3826–924.

rationale: Base emergency-laparotomy case: frail, elderly, anticoagulated and septic. Tests emergency level, sepsis alarm, antibiotics, source control, critical care, risk scoring, frailty assessment, geriatric input, shared decision-making and the DOAC plan.
